NDT training on the West Coast: how it works

Short answer: On the West Coast you study NDT theory online at your own pace on the Atlantis portal, with an ASNT NDT Level III answering your questions, then do the hands-on training and practical examination at your employer's shop, yard or plant under a written practice built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. The employer, not the course, certifies you. Atlantis NDT has no classroom on the West Coast; its offices are in Houston, Texas and Hyderabad, India.

That model fits the way the coast hires. Shipyards in San Diego and on Puget Sound, refineries in the Los Angeles basin and around San Francisco Bay, and aerospace plants from Everett to El Segundo each run their own qualification programme, and each expects a new technician to arrive with the theory done and the hours documented. Course access opens the moment you enrol, in any month, so the theory can be finished between shifts or before a start date. The published US course fees on this page cover Level I and Level II in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, and the national picture is on NDT training in the USA.

Where NDT technicians work across the West Coast

Navy shipbuilding and repair in San Diego. General Dynamics NASSCO builds and repairs Navy and commercial ships on San Diego Bay, and Naval Base San Diego homeports a large part of the Pacific surface fleet, which keeps ship repair contracts flowing to private yards and subcontractors. Repair contractors examine welds and structure under NAVSEA requirements, so visual, magnetic particle, penetrant and ultrasonic work make up most of the day. See NDT training in San Diego.

Puget Sound and Columbia River yards. Puget Sound Naval Shipyard in Bremerton maintains and overhauls Navy ships, including nuclear-powered carriers and submarines, and qualifies its own federal inspection workforce. Private yards in Seattle, Tacoma and Portland repair ferries, fishing vessels, tugs, barges and government ships, usually to classification-society rules and Coast Guard requirements. That private work is where most outside trainees log their supervised hours. See Seattle, Tacoma and Portland.

Aerospace manufacture. Boeing builds commercial airplanes at Everett and Renton, and a large supplier base across western Washington machines, bonds and assembles parts for those lines. Southern California carries airframe, defense and space manufacturing around El Segundo, Long Beach, Torrance and the Antelope Valley. Aerospace NDT here is penetrant, magnetic particle, ultrasonic and eddy current work to the customer's specifications, and technicians are certified under the employer's written practice, built on SNT-TC-1A and aligned with the prime's flow-down and Nadcap AC7114. See El Segundo, Long Beach and Los Angeles.

Refining and terminals. California's refineries sit in two clusters, the Los Angeles basin (El Segundo, Torrance, Wilmington, Carson) and the northeast shore of San Francisco Bay (Richmond, Martinez, Benicia, Rodeo); Washington's are in the north Sound at Anacortes and near Ferndale. In-service work at these plants means ultrasonic thickness readings on piping circuits, weld examination during turnarounds and tank inspection at the terminals. The California base is shrinking: Phillips 66 announced the closure of its Los Angeles-area refinery, Valero announced the end of refining at Benicia, and other units have moved to renewable fuels. Shutdown, demolition and conversion projects still need examination, but they favor technicians who can move between plants. See Martinez, San Francisco and California.

Oilfields and pipelines. Kern County around Bakersfield is California's main producing area, with gathering lines, steam generators and tank batteries to examine. In Alaska, North Slope production moves south through the Trans-Alaska Pipeline System to the Valdez terminal, and Anchorage is where crews stage for the slope. See Bakersfield and Anchorage.

Nuclear power and Hanford. Energy Northwest's Columbia Generating Station near Richland and PG&E's Diablo Canyon in California bring refueling outages with in-service inspection to ASME Section XI. The Hanford cleanup site beside Richland adds tank, piping and waste-treatment plant work under Department of Energy quality rules. See Richland.

Ports, bridges and seismic steel. The container ports at Los Angeles and Long Beach, Oakland and Seattle–Tacoma run cranes, wharves and terminal steel that need structural examination. Buildings and bridges on the coast are designed for earthquakes: after the 1994 Northridge earthquake cracked welded steel moment connections, seismic weld requirements tightened, and AWS D1.8 now supplements AWS D1.1 for seismic force-resisting systems. Ultrasonic testing of complete-joint-penetration welds and magnetic particle testing of connections are routine on those projects.

Which NDT methods and levels West Coast employers ask for

West Coast employers hire Level II technicians to run examinations and accept results, and Level I trainees to assist while they log hours. The table pairs each sector with the methods it relies on and the documents that set acceptance.

SectorMethods employers ask forCodes and documents that govern acceptance
Navy ship repair (San Diego, Puget Sound)VT, MT, PT, UT; RT by licensed crewsNAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 for method and personnel requirements, MIL-STD-2035 for acceptance
Commercial ship repair and ferriesUT thickness gauging, VT, MTClassification-society rules, U.S. Coast Guard requirements
Refining and terminalsUT thickness, VT, PT, MT, RT; PAUT on weldsAPI 510, API 570, API 653, ASME B31.3, ASME Section V
Aerospace manufacturePT, MT, UT, ET, VTCustomer specifications, ASTM E1417 (PT), ASTM E1444 (MT), Nadcap AC7114
Seismic structural steelVT, UT, MTAWS D1.1, AWS D1.8, the project's building-code inspection programme
Nuclear outagesUT, VT, PT, ETASME Section XI; performance demonstration for most UT
Oilfield and pipelinesVT, RT, UT, MTAPI 1104, 49 CFR Part 192 and Part 195

For a new entrant, VT, PT and MT build the base and lead to paid work in fabrication and ship repair; UT opens the refining, aerospace and structural markets. The ultrasonic testing training page sets out the UT path by level, and the NDT Level 1 training and NDT Level 2 training pages explain what each level lets you do on the job.

How NDT certification works across West Coast state lines

No West Coast state licenses NDT technicians by method. California, Oregon, Washington and Alaska leave certification to the employer, and the common basis is ASNT SNT-TC-1A, a recommended practice that each employer turns into its own written practice. That document fixes the training hours, experience, examinations and vision checks for every method and level, and the employer signs the certification.

The consequence for anyone who relocates is plain: your certification belongs to the company that issued it. A technician who leaves a San Diego repair contractor for a Puget Sound fabricator brings training records, logged hours and examination history, but the new employer recertifies under its own written practice, normally with fresh specific and practical examinations and a vision test. Complete records make that quick; missing records can mean repeating hours, so keep signed copies of everything.

The portable alternative is ASNT central certification, which belongs to the technician. At Level III, the ASNT NDT Level III certificate is widely used as the examination basis for an employer's Level III certification, and it moves with you from job to job. Atlantis prepares candidates for those examinations; ASNT runs them. Check where you stand with the SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker.

Sector programmes add their own layer. Navy repair brings NAVSEA personnel requirements that the employer's programme and Level III must meet. Nuclear utilities add ASME Section XI Appendix VIII performance demonstration for most ultrasonic examinations, plus their own access programmes. Aerospace primes flow qualification requirements down through the purchase order. None of these replaces the employer's written practice; each sits on top of it. Employers who need that document drafted or brought up to date can use our written practice development service.

Industrial radiography licensing in California, Oregon, Washington and Alaska

Radiation safety is regulated separately from NDT certification, and an RT course licenses nobody. California, Oregon and Washington are NRC Agreement States, so their own agencies license industrial radiography: the California Department of Public Health's Radiologic Health Branch, the Oregon Health Authority's Radiation Protection Services and the Washington State Department of Health's Office of Radiation Protection. Alaska is not an Agreement State, so radioactive-material licences for radiography there come from the NRC.

Federal rules in 10 CFR Part 34, and the matching state rules, require a radiographer to complete radiation-safety training, pass a radiographer certification examination and follow the licensee's operating and emergency procedures, while an assistant works only under a radiographer's personal supervision. A company licensed in one state applies for reciprocity before sending a crew into another. Most West Coast radiographers therefore hold two qualifications: the radiation-safety credential tied to the licence, and the employer's SNT-TC-1A RT certification covering technique and interpretation. Atlantis does not perform radiography in the United States; our radiographic testing training covers technique, image quality and interpretation, not licensing.

Choosing an NDT training provider on the West Coast

West Coast candidates have four broad routes, and the right one depends on whether you already have an employer.

  • Full-time schools with labs. These programmes put you in front of equipment and specimens from the start. They suit someone with no NDT employer yet, at the cost of time away from paid work.
  • Community and technical college programmes. Some colleges teach NDT or welding inspection over one or two years, often alongside welding. They give the broadest grounding and the slowest route to a first certification.
  • Trainee positions with an employer. Inspection companies and shipyards hire helpers and trainees, then send them through formal training while they log hours. Ask how the formal hours will be delivered and recorded.
  • Self-paced online theory plus a practical at the employer. This is the Atlantis model: theory online with Level III support, practice in a simulator, then hands-on training and examination at the employer's facility on its equipment. It suits people already employed or holding a confirmed offer, and companies training staff without taking them off the job.

Whatever you choose, ask the same questions. Do the hours meet the employer's written practice? Who conducts the practical examination, and on what specimens? Which records will you receive, and will a future employer accept them? Does the course certify you, or prepare you for certification by an employer? The honest answer to the last one is always the second. The national NDT training page and the NDT training FAQ answer these questions for Atlantis courses.

Training a crew across several West Coast sites

A contractor with technicians in San Diego, the Bay Area and Puget Sound needs one programme, not three. That starts with a single written practice covering every method and technique the crews use and every customer overlay they work under. Theory goes online, so a technician on nights in Anacortes and one on days in Long Beach finish the same material on their own schedules.

The hands-on part comes to you. An ASNT NDT Level III certified in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, with 11+ years of field experience, trains and examines at your facility on your instruments, procedures and representative parts, so the specific and practical examinations test the work your crews actually do. You end up with a certification file built to your written practice, with training hours, experience logs, examination grades and vision records ready for a customer audit. Send your sites, methods, levels and head-count through the training enquiry form. We reply within one business day.

Practise before your practical examination

The practical examination is where candidates lose marks: calibration steps skipped, scan coverage left incomplete, indications described loosely. Practical NDT lets you rehearse in a 3D simulator that runs in a browser, on a PC or in VR, following a twelve-step procedure in which the evaluator credits only what you record. The UT simulator and the process-plant workplace match refinery and terminal jobs; the welding workshop matches fabrication and ship repair. Simulator time makes the procedure familiar; certification still rests on supervised hours, a hands-on practical examination and the employer's signature.

For the written examinations, the free Level II practice tests cover general and specific questions method by method.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training on the West Coast

How long does NDT training take on the West Coast?

Formal training is counted in hours per method and level, set by the employer's written practice from the SNT-TC-1A recommendations, so the time depends on those hours and on how much study you fit around work. Supervised experience takes longer than the coursework. The training requirements matrix lists the recommended hours by method.

Can I train online from California, Oregon or Washington?

Yes for the theory: the course runs on the Atlantis portal and opens when you enrol. The hands-on training and practical examination happen in person at the employer's facility, because certification needs supervised work on real equipment. See NDT training online.

Is there an NDT training center near me in Seattle, Los Angeles or San Diego?

Not one run by Atlantis. The pages for Southern California and the Pacific Northwest describe the local markets, and for employers the training travels to the facility rather than the other way round.

Which NDT method should I learn first?

Start with what your target employer uses. VT plus PT or MT suits fabrication shops and ship repair; UT is the method refineries, aerospace plants and structural inspectors hire for, and it takes longer to learn. Many technicians add UT once they hold a surface method.

Does my certification move with me if I relocate from Washington to California?

Not by itself. SNT-TC-1A certification is issued by your employer, so a new employer recertifies you under its written practice using your records. ASNT central certification is the credential that travels with you.

How do I become an NDT Level III on the West Coast?

Level III candidates usually pass the ASNT Basic examination and a method examination, then are certified by their employer. Our ASNT Level III training is self-paced preparation for those examinations, with Level III support for your questions.

Is an AWS CWI the same as NDT certification?

No. The Certified Welding Inspector credential covers welding inspection and is issued by AWS after its examination; NDT certification covers specific test methods. Atlantis offers six-day AWS CWI exam prep as corporate training at your facility, online, or one-to-one online or in person, with city pages for Los Angeles, San Diego and Seattle.
